prompt: Prime-time adult animated sitcom characters, simple rounded people with big round eyes, small dot pupils and overbites, flat colour and black outlines everywhere except the faces, which are rendered with startling real skin: pores, stubble, sweat, tired wet eyes. Every flat colour is laid on with thick visible oil brushstrokes. Only the bodies, clothes and places are cartoon: every face in the frame, however small, is painted as real human skin with wrinkles, pores, bags under the eyes and real eyelids, far more lifelike than anything around it, and no feature is exaggerated. Close on the face of a tiny white grandmother in her eighties in a freezing 1930s attic at night: thin silver hair in a hairnet, a long pointed nose, a mole on one cheek, frost on her eyelashes and eyebrows, lips blue, mouth open in a long shivering wail, a big cloud of breath steaming out into the cold air. She clutches three cardigans and a crocheted blanket to her chin. The warm glow of one candle lights her face from below; behind her, icicles hang from the roof beams in cold blue dark. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
